issues.description: New AWS client created per LLMContextFrame causes overhead and resource churn
issues.detail: process_frame opens a fresh aioboto3 client inside an async-with for every incoming context frame. Client construction does TLS, endpoint resolution, and credential loading on each invocation. For a conversational pipeline this is expensive and hurts latency. Create the client once during setup or lazily cache it on first use.

issues.description: Naming convention violation: agentArn is camelCase in a public Python API
issues.detail: The constructor parameter agentArn (and self._agentArn) breaks PEP 8 and the rest of the file's snake_case convention (aws_access_key, aws_region). This is a public API; renaming later is a breaking change. Use agent_arn before merging.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer raises on non-JSON lines, killing the stream
issues.detail: json.loads(response_line) is unguarded. If AgentCore emits a keepalive, comment, or malformed line, JSONDecodeError will propagate out of process_frame and abort the response. Wrap in try/except returning None, or validate before parsing. Currently the warning path for malformed 'data:' prefixes is logged but JSON failure crashes the pipeline.

issues.description: Class name mismatches PR title and docstring (Bedrock vs non-Bedrock)
issues.detail: PR title says AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor but the class is AWSAgentCoreProcessor; module docstring also says AWSAgentCoreProcessor. Pick one canonical name now; renaming after release breaks imports. Also confirm __init__'s `from .agent_core import *` exports the intended symbol.

issues.description: Class-attribute _output_response_open is shared state across concurrent invocations
issues.detail: If two LLMContextFrames arrive before the first completes (or timeout closes), the bookend logic races: _output_response_open, _close_task, and _last_text_frame_time are not guarded by a lock. This can emit unmatched Start/End frames or double-cancel tasks. Consider a lock or an explicit per-invocation state machine.

issues.description: Non-streaming part splitting assumes newline-terminated SSE; trailing whitespace lines ignored silently
issues.detail: When is_multi_part_response is true, part_string.split('\n') will include partial lines if SSE chunks split mid-line across parts. Each part is decoded independently, so a 'data: foo' broken across two parts becomes two warnings and dropped text. Buffer across parts until a blank line per SSE spec, or document the limitation.

review.summary: The new AWSAgentCoreProcessor has solid intent but several issues to address before merge. The most actionable items are the camelCase agentArn parameter (public API naming), per-frame AWS client creation, unguarded json.loads in the default response transformer, and a name mismatch between the PR title/docstring and the actual class. Concurrency state for response bookends is also fragile if context frames overlap. SSE parsing assumes a single part contains whole lines, which may drop tokens.
